title: 200 :hover rules with descendant effects vs none, under a pointer sweep
variable: :hover rules present vs absent while the pointer moves
claim: Antipattern #28 from web-performance-antipatterns-50.md: ':hover/:focus-within rules with descendant effects on many elements - pointer movement triggers subtree recalcs.' Hover states are unavoidable in menu-driven game UI, and the expensive form is the one tested here: a hover rule that restyles descendants rather than the hovered element itself, so entering an element invalidates a subtree.
result: CONFIRMED, and it scales: no reliable difference at 30 elements, Styles 1.16x at 100, 2.47x at 300, measured under a real pointer sweep. Hover rules whose effect reaches descendants do cost styling time as the pointer crosses them, and the cost grows with how many hoverable elements exist rather than with how many are actually under the cursor. Note the :focus-within half of the antipattern is N/A - cohtml rejects that pseudo entirely.
notes: Applicability gate: ADAPTED. :hover is supported. :focus-within is NOT - the feature inventory records it as a rejected pseudo ('unsupported pseudo: :focus-within'), so the second half of the antipattern is N/A in Gameface and only the :hover half is measurable. THE OTHER ADAPTATION: a hover case is worthless without a moving pointer, and the lab had no way to produce one. Input.dispatchMouseEvent turned out to work against the Player (it is not listed by Schema.getDomains, but neither is Tracing) and was verified to drive :hover - a dispatched move changed a :hover-only width from 100px to 300px and fired a mouseover handler. The runner now supports an 'input: pointer-sweep' field, which walks the pointer along a fixed deterministic path at a fixed rate, starting before the warmup so hover state is in its steady rhythm before tracing opens. The path uses coprime strides over the viewport, so it is identical in both variants and has no randomness. Rule 1: one variable, the presence of the 200 :hover rules. Rule 2: identical DOM - every tile has the .inner child in both variants, so B's descendant effect has the same subtree to reach that A's rules ignore. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4: no text, no assets. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080, and the sweep covers that area. Rule 6: the pointer sweep is the churn and runs from before load; the shared root-nudge driver also runs so both variants re-render regardless of where the pointer is. Rule 7: the sweep path is deterministic. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is Styles. Generated by tools/make-rule-heavy-cases.js.
